The stated kinetic and gradient positivity conditions hold on that branch. The d=0 degeneracy and strong-coupling behavior require separate analysis.

records.claim: Reconstructed finite deterministic test-star: q>=2, states x_1,...,x_q,L,H; initially only H observed as 1. T_j sends x_j to H, all other x_i to L; L,H absorbing. With the same unknown state on each copy, exact pooled one-copy response rank is q+2, whereas one adaptive k-copy protocol has maximal coherent rank min(q+2,k+2). Thus k_rank=1 and zero-error identification needs q copies. Uniform prior residual entropy for 0<=k<=q is (q-k+1)/(q+2) log2(q-k+1). Cycling candidates and using one destructive test generates the same test family with two actions.
records.verification: Accessible handoff baseline contains explicit reconstruction rather than the missing original A005 standalone file. No new execution or formal proof audit. Scope limited to the stipulated deterministic observations and copy regime; not a general no-cloning result.

claims: Noninjectivity of f on all states need not imply distinguishability loss on a restricted accessible family: f(0)=0,f(1)=1,f(2)=0 is injective on {0,1} but not {0,2}.
A three-cycle can be reversed by a tailored involution but not by an independently fixed identity reversal; distinguish abstract reversibility from a prescribed physical reversal.

An environment with one bit of capacity for a two-state reset need not carry one bit of entropy: for P(X=1)=.01 the record entropy is h2(.01)≈.0807931 bits; heat requires additional thermodynamic assumptions.

A deterministic bit-flip instrument realizing the unit effect need not satisfy 1∘b=b, so arbitrary instruments do not automatically satisfy the sequential-product axioms used in Jordan reconstruction.

records.claim: For K merging the first two coordinates of a classical three-outcome distribution, p=(.5,.3,.2), q=(.2,.2,.6) preserve TV=.4 but their unique linear two-output recovery has a negative entry; the reported minimax TV error is 1/30. For p=(.5,.5,0), q=(0,.5,.5) and the same merge, TV is preserved and the reported minimax error is 1/6. No universal zero-deficit TV-to-recovery implication.
records.verification: Source secondary review reports 22/22 checks including LP calculations; not independently replayed in this intake. No claim that 1/6 is the global optimum across all systems.

records.claim: Under common compatible affine data and common affine gates preserving both compact convex normalized bases B_-⊊B_+, B_t=(1-t)B_-+t B_+ supplies continuum many compatible invariant bases. Support functions distinguish t. If fixed preparations affinely span the relevant space, a data-preserving affine map fixing them must be identity. Exact recovery under K=id does not resolve cone-completion ambiguity.

records.claim: For nonempty S=Sol(Psi) of a satisfiable Boolean 2-CNF, XOR translation stabilizer equals intersection of pullbacks of stabilizers of all unary and pairwise coordinate projections. Each stabilizer is a linear subspace over F2, hence Sym(S)=ker H. Reverse inclusion follows from clause locality and the XOR involution. For S={00,11}, translations 10 and 01 are individually nonsymmetries, yet their XOR 11 is a symmetry: individual negative witnesses on a basis do not certify that its span contains no symmetry.
records.verification: Read informal proof and inspected and reran the supplied standard-library test in a temporary directory. Both unittest cases passed (includes exhaustive nonempty 2-CNF solution relations for n=1,2,3). Not a formal theorem certificate or a new general complexity result. P versus NP remains OPEN.
